newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish shares firm, helped by Dow strength.
newsitem.headline: Irish shares firm, helped by Dow strength.

text.p: Irish shares firmed in morning trade on Wednesday, benefiting from overnight gains on the Dow, but dealers said trading had been fairly light.
Upbeat comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan helped the Dow power ahead to record levels on Tuesday and most European bourses followed suit in early trade on Wednesday.
"We are obviously firmer on the back of New York. Dublin has marked up but trading has been light so far and everyone is watching sterling," one dealer said.
Sterling surged to fresh highs above 3.08 marks in morning trade on Wednesday, forcing the punt/sterling rate to seven-year lows below 88 pence.
"That is helping to drive up Irish prices," one trader noted.
By 0920 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was up 21.04 points or 0.59 percent at 3,605.33.
The main banking stocks, Allied Irish Banks and Bank of Ireland gained seven pence to 588 and 827 respectively.
Irish Life and Irish Permanent firmed five pence to 375 and 660 respectively while Anglo Irish Bank was up a penny at 94 and insurer Hibernian added five pence to 390.
Among industrial stocks, CRH gained nine pence to 689, Smurfit was up a penny at 220 while Irish Continental Group added 10 pence to 770.
